title: Master, stacked and combined graphs
copy: One definition binds the master, a service view and a business view that consumes both.

title: Consume an input stream
copy: Supply events or batches through the same async port. Handle each receipt.

title: Observe graph commits
copy: The graph feed carries snapshots, commits, progress and gaps.

title: Adapt Hubble records
copy: Pass native records and their versioned mapping to an injected adapter.

title: Put data on an edge
copy: An observed call has an identity, endpoints, a type and a health property.

title: Resolve a stable identity
copy: Use the tenant, cluster and Kubernetes UID as the object key.

title: Declare a property
copy: The ontology decides which values a property accepts.

title: Match a graph pattern
copy: Bind the service endpoints and their observed call.

title: Validate a composition
copy: Compile the whole graph space before installing its definitions.

title: Combine compatible rows
copy: Both branches must supply the same typed endpoint-pair shape.

title: Aggregate dependency health
copy: Group by service and ask whether any dependency has failed.

title: Batch and compose ordered patches
copy: A batch keeps event boundaries. Ordered composition checks adjacent revisions.

title: Subtract deltas, then choose a base
copy: Signed arithmetic and patch conversion are separate typed requests.

title: Read a finite neighborhood
copy: Pin a graph revision, scope and work budget for stored or virtual data.

title: Bound a traversal
copy: Follow Calls for up to four hops. Fixed-point recursion has additional requirements.

title: Record a correspondence
copy: Connect a source deployment to a distinct target capability.

title: Propose a backward edit
copy: Use an explicitly bidirectional rule and its versioned context.

title: Replace a projection definition
copy: An expected version guards the configuration edit.

title: Project and render Markdown
copy: Pass the returned typed snapshot to a renderer. Keep its source revisions.

title: Build and verify the design
copy: Run from the extracted sattle-design folder with .NET 10 and Python installed.
text:
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 tools/verify.py
note: This builds the contracts and caller examples, then runs the finite model and selected schema/compiler checks. It does not execute a production engine.
